title: Warmer Colours Only
tests: Tests interpreting 'warmer' as a colour-temperature adjustment rather than a scene or weather change.

faults.what: The warming is excessive: a strong orange-yellow cast overwhelms the scene's natural colours, making it look heavily filtered rather than simply warmer.
Deepened shadows obscure detail in the foreground branches, shoreline rocks and forest, especially on the right.

judge.summary: The composition and reflections are preserved, but the extreme orange treatment and darkened shadows need toning down.

must_haves.item: The image has a visibly warmer colour balance than the source.
must_haves.why: The blue-toned source has been shifted strongly toward orange and yellow.

must_haves.item: The same mountains, pine trees, clouds and lake remain in their original positions.
must_haves.why: The visible scene elements retain their original shapes and placement.

must_haves.item: The lake's reflections and surface details retain their original structure.
must_haves.why: The reflected mountains, trees and clouds, along with the ripple patterns, remain aligned with the source.

must_haves.item: No sun, sunset, extra clouds or other scene elements are added.
must_haves.why: No new scene elements are visible; the sunset-like appearance comes from recolouring the existing image.

must_haves.item: Framing, geometry and image detail remain unchanged apart from colour.
must_haves.why: Framing and geometry are preserved, but the darker shadow treatment reduces visible detail in the trees and foreground.
